Detects the anomaly and identifies the spike level and the metric that exceeded the threshold.\\\\n\\\\n2. Correlates source activity, analyzes Amazon Bedrock invocation patterns, identifies which models received elevated traffic, and quantifies token consumption.\\\\n\\\\n3. Checks for contributing factors, and then reviews CloudTrail for recent deployments, configuration changes, or new IAM activity that correlates with the spike timing.\\\\n\\\\n4. Rules out infrastructure issues, and confirms whether throttling, errors, or latency contributed to the spike.\\\\n\\\\n5. Delivers root causes and mitigation and provides specific remediation steps.\\\\n\\\\nIn the previous example use case, DevOps Agent identifies the summarization service as the source and traces the spike to the deployment that removed the token quota. Then, it quantifies that the impact is 2 million tokens in 30 minutes. Finally, Dev Ops Agent recommends rolling back the change and adding [Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.html) for token budget enforcement.\\\\n\\\\n![DevOps Agent investigation that shows symptom detection and root cause identification](/media/postImages/original/IM7WVYD6QmRNm3y84ZIuy3UQ)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/AR_gbMkpbaTJOwRyCpqGf6uA/analyze-amazon-bedrock-cost-spikes-with-aws-devops-agent\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Use AWS DevOps Agent to triage and route AWS Health event impact | AWS Cloud Operations Blog\",\"context\":\"### Validate the results\\\\n\\\\nWith a test event in flight, you can watch each stage of the pipeline and confirm it produced the right output.\\\\n\\\\nStart in the AWS Step Functions console. Open the state machine created by the stack and select the most recent execution. Watch it move from the investigation trigger, through the wait-for-task-token state, to the `Has Findings?` choice state. A successful run ends in a `Succeeded` state, and for a confirmed-impact event it passes through the `CreateOpsItem` and notification states rather than the no-impact branch.\\\\n\\\\nFigure 2: Step Functions execution moving through the investigation trigger, the wait-for-task-token state, and the impact decision.\\\\n\\\\nNext, open the investigation in the AWS DevOps Agent operator app. The investigation for your test event shows its status, and as it runs you can watch the agent work through the impact-assessment skill against your topology.\\\\n\\\\nFigure 3: An investigation starting in the AWS DevOps Agent operator app.\\\\n\\\\nAs the investigation proceeds, the agent applies the skill\u2019s methodology step by step, listing the affected workloads, the severity it assigned to each, and the teams it identified from resource tags.\\\\n\\\\nFigure 4: The agent applying the impact-assessment skill against the discovered application topology.\\\\n\\\\nThe operator app also gives you a dashboard view of past and in-progress investigations, so you can see how the agent has triaged events over time.\\\\n\\\\nFigure 5: The AWS DevOps Agent dashboard listing past and in-progress investigations.\\\\n\\\\nFinally, confirm the tracking record in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Open OpsCenter and find the new OpsItem for the event. Confirm that its severity matches the investigation priority, its status is `Open`, and its description carries the agent\u2019s summary, findings, recommendations, and a link back to the investigation. The same details reach the owning teams through the channels you configured: an email from the Amazon SNS topic, plus a Slack or Microsoft Teams message for any team whose `notifyOn` list includes the event\u2019s severity.\\\\n\\\\nFigure 6: The OpsCenter OpsItem carrying the agent\u2019s severity, summary, findings, and a link to the investigation\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/use-aws-devops-agent-to-triage-and-route-aws-health-event-impact/\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Monitoring production agent lifecycle with AWS DevOps Agent and AgentCore Evaluations | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"### Layer 2: AWS DevOps Agent, is the system healthy?\\\\n\\\\nAgentCore Evaluations monitors agent quality, but infrastructure issues like permissions and tool errors need a different approach. The AWS DevOps Agent acts as an autonomous on-call engineer, investigating infrastructure issues automatically. When anomalies occur, it analyzes system logs, infrastructure metrics, and error patterns, then provides specific remediation steps.\\\\n\\\\nThe following demo video (Video 2) showcases how the AWS DevOps Agent can be triggered through a signed webhook for the Travel Agent:\\\\n\\\\n[](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/artifacts/DBSBlogs/ML-20434/devops_blogpost_final.mp4?_=2)\\\\n\\\\n*Video 2: How the AWS DevOps Agent performs an investigation, looking into relevant Amazon CloudWatch logs and AWS service gaps to identify the root cause and provide remediation steps*\\\\n\\\\nAs shown in the video, after an incident is submitted through a signed webhook, the AWS DevOps Agent first identifies relevant logs from Amazon CloudWatch, then analyzes it to check for common errors such as IAM permission issues, tool failures or other hidden errors, and finally applies large language model (LLM)-based reasoning to identify a root cause and targeted recommendations to help prevent the issue in the future.\\\\n\\\\nWithout the AWS DevOps Agent, you would see that the airline swarm agent suddenly stopped responding to flight booking requests, returning either a generic error message or a completely blank output instead of helping the user.\\\\n\\\\nAt this point, you would:\\\\n\\\\n1. Check application logs for error patterns.\\\\n2. Review recent deployments for potential causes.\\\\n3. Examine IAM policies and permissions manually.\\\\n4. Correlate Amazon CloudWatch metrics across multiple services.\\\\n5. Trace the execution flow through multiple agent interactions.\\\\n\\\\nThis process could take 30\u201360 minutes, assuming there is a deep knowledge of the system architecture.\\\\n\\\\nAfter we submitted the incident directly to our AWS DevOps Agent Space through a signed webhook connected to the AWS DevOps Agent Space, an investigation was kicked off, resulting in a topology graph of the affected AWS resources as well as a comprehensive analysis of the Amazon CloudWatch logs from the AgentCore runtime.\\\\n\\\\n[](https://d2908q01vomqb2.cloudfront.net/f1f836cb4ea6efb2a0b1b99f41ad8b103eff4b59/2026/08/31/ML-20434-12.jpg)\\\\n\\\\nFigure 7\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/monitoring-production-agent-lifecycle-with-aws-devops-agent-and-agentcore-evaluations/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Customers \u2013 AWS DevOps Agent \u2013 AWS\",\"context\":\"## Infor\\\\n\\\\n\\\\\"AWS DevOps Agent is helping us transform how we investigate and resolve infrastructure issues. The agent\\'s prevention-based analysis identified patterns across incidents and recommends improvements before issues reach production. This shifts us from reactive firefighting to proactive optimization. During preview testing in a test environment, the agent successfully diagnosed mismatched VPN PSKs, routing misconfigurations, CloudFormation failures, and performance issues with minimal input. Its deep technical analysis examines not just symptoms but underlying patterns across network, application and infrastructure layers. The integrations with CloudWatch logs, automated Skills creation, and learned topology discovery will accelerate our DevOps practices significantly.\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n**- Jim Plourde, EVP Cloud Services, Infor**\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/devops-agent/customers/\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"AWS DevOps Agent\",\"context\":\"## Overview of AWS DevOps Agent\\\\n\\\\nAWS DevOps Agent is a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) powered service that helps\\\\nsoftware engineering teams investigate production incidents, optimize operational health, and\\\\ngenerate prevention recommendations based on historical incidents. The service uses AI agents to\\\\nautomatically analyze observability signals, correlate telemetry with code and deployment data,\\\\nidentify root causes of incidents, and provide actionable recommendations to resolve issues.\\\\nAWS DevOps Agent operates within Agent Spaces: customer defined scoped environments that define\\\\nwhat resources and services the AI agents can access. Each Agent Space maintains a\\\\ntopology\u2014a knowledge graph of the application environment\u2014serving as the foundation\\\\nfor intelligent incident investigation and analysis. The service integrates with observability\\\\ntools, code repositories and CI/CD pipelines, and incident management tools. Customers can also\\\\nextend AWS DevOps Agent by securely connecting to private or remote MCP (Model Context Protocol)\\\\nservers. For more information, see the AWS DevOps Agent User Guide.\\\\n\\\\nWe assess the quality of AWS DevOps Agent by measuring how well the agent\\'s outputs align with\\\\nground-truth expectations defined for known incident scenarios. For incident investigations, we\\\\nevaluate whether the agent correctly identifies the root cause of an incident by comparing\\\\ninvestigation findings against known root causes. For prevention recommendations, we evaluate\\\\noutputs across two levels. A recommendation is considered \\\\\"valid\\\\\" if it is assessed as meeting\\\\nboth safety criteria (following the recommendation would not worsen the operational situation)\\\\nand correctness criteria (the proposed solution is technically sound). A recommendation is\\\\nconsidered \\\\\"high-value\\\\\" if, in addition to being valid, it also demonstrates goal focus (targets\\\\nthe specific problem rather than generic advice), actionability (an engineer can execute the\\\\nrecommendation without ambiguity), and evidence quality (cites specific observability data from\\\\nthe customer\\'s environment). AWS DevOps Agent does not provide a confidence score for its outputs;\\\\na customer\\'s workflow must decide if an investigation finding or recommendation is effective\\\\nusing human judgment\u2014for example, by reviewing the cited evidence and validating findings\\\\nbefore taking remediation actions.\\\\n\\\\nAs is the case with more traditional ML solutions, AWS DevOps Agent must overcome issues of\\\\nintrinsic and confounding variation. Intrinsic variation refers to features of the input\\\\nenvironment to which the agent must attend\u2014for example, different application\\\\narchitectures (monolithic vs. microservices), different root causes of incidents (code regression\\\\nvs. configuration change vs. infrastructure\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ai/responsible-ai/aws-aidevops-agent/overview.html\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be.
